`insight:promoter-pledge-group-contagion` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Indian blow-ups repeatedly ran through promoter-level leverage rather than the listed company's own P&L: Zee/Essel (pledge 59% -> ~90%, promoter stake ~42% -> ~4%), ADAG (near-100% pledges; RCap, RCom, RHFL), Future Group (FRL promoter stake 47% -> 14% via invocations), Satyam (promoter stake ~25% -> ~8.6%, pledged), Kingfisher/UB (cross-guarantees), Cox & Kings. Mechanism: falling price -> margin call -> lenders invoke and dump shares -> further fall (reflexive), often triggered by a credit event elsewhere (IL&FS Sep 2018 froze MF/NBFC lending against shares). Signals: pledge % of promoter holding (disclosed quarterly under SAST; 'encumbrance' incl. non-disposal undertakings); rising pledge while price rises = borrowing against inflated value; listed company guarantees, letters of comfort, FDs or ICDs to group entities; MF/NBFC 'loan against shares' exposure to the group; promoter selling via 'gifts' or off-market transfers (PC Jeweller). Rules: pledge >25% of promoter holding or any rising trend = disqualifier for long-term holding; check all group listed companies, not just the one you own -- contagion is group-wide (Essel, ADAG, Future, IL&FS). SEBI disclosure since 2019 includes encumbrance reasons; track quarterly.

**Links:** part_of -> `insight:disqualifiers`
**Sources:** <https://business-standard.com/article/pf/zee-stock-crash-shows-why-you-should-avoid-firms-with-high-pledged-shares-119013100051_1.html> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/future-group-shareholders-stare-at-possible-wipeout-of-investments-122042400555_1.html> ; <https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/company-stock/story/zee-shares-hit-over-6yr-low-as-promoters-increase-pledge-to-90-rebounds-debt-repayment-plan-231895-2019-10-07>

`case_study:dominos-2008-2021` · tickers US-DPZ · confidence: verified

IPO July 2004 at $14. Highly levered (securitised debt), it hit ~$3 in Nov 2008 [unverified] and was in the low single digits in early 2009. Dec 2009: CEO-elect Patrick Doyle (CEO Mar 2010) launched the ~$75m 'Pizza Turnaround' campaign on camera admitting customers found the pizza poor, with a new recipe; same-store sales jumped ~14% in Q1 2010 [unverified]. Then a digital-first strategy (Pizza Tracker 2008, online/app ordering, later >half of US sales digital), store remodels, and a 'fortressing' franchise model. Under Doyle the stock rose ~13x (Restaurant Business); Quartz noted it beat Google's return from 2010. Peak ~$567 (Dec 2021) [unverified] ≈ ~180x from the 2008 low, ~65x from 2010. Split: mostly EPS + aggressive buybacks/recaps (negative equity, share count down); P/E moved from ~10x to ~30x+ [unverified]. Drawdown: ~-80% 2007-08 pre-turnaround [unverified]; -~35% 2022. EARLY SIGNAL visible in 2010: the honest relaunch produced an immediate double-digit same-store-sales jump — a measurable demand response — at a ~10x P/E. Who caught it: few documented; later Berkshire Hathaway disclosed a DPZ stake (Q3 2024). Stall: 2022-26 range-bound as US delivery competition and aggregators matured. LESSON: in a franchise model, a product reset that shows up in same-store sales within one quarter, plus leverage-funded buybacks, can produce a 100x; check the first comp print.

- **Start → end:** ~$3 (Nov 2008) [unverified] → ~$567 (Dec 2021) [unverified] (~180x from trough; ~13x under Doyle)
- **EPS vs rerating:** mostly EPS + buybacks; some rerating
- **Max drawdown:** ~-80% pre-2009 [unverified]
- **Early signal:** Q1 2010 same-store sales jump after honest relaunch; digital ordering share
- **Who caught it:** few documented; Berkshire 2024 (late)
- **Ended/stalled:** range-bound 2022-26
- **Lesson:** first comp print after product reset is the signal
- **Sources:** [1](https://qz.com/885979/in-2010-dominos-dpz-admitted-it-made-terrible-pizza-now-its-stock-returns-have-outpaced-googles-googl-goog-in-one-measurement) · [2](https://restaurantbusinessonline.com/financing/five-lessons-dominos-comeback) · [3](https://www.fool.com/investing/2019/11/19/the-secret-behind-dominos-epic-turnaround.aspx) · [4](https://www.nrn.com/people/patrick-doyle-leaves-legacy-success-domino-s)

`theme:sector-pharma-cdmo` · confidence: single-source · tickers: SUNPHARMA, DRREDDY, CIPLA, LUPIN, ZYDUSLIFE, TORNTPHARM, DIVISLAB, SYNGENE

**How it makes money:** US generics (limited-competition launches), India branded (doctor franchise), API (cost/chemistry), CDMO (innovator contracts).

**Metrics that matter:**
- US sales $ and QoQ price erosion
- ANDA filings/approvals, complex pipeline
- USFDA status of key sites (OAI/WL/import alert)
- India growth vs IPM
- R&D % of sales
- EBITDA margin ex-one-offs
- CDMO: order book, molecules in Phase III/commercial

**Value chain and where margins sit:** KSM/intermediates (China-dominated) -> API -> formulation -> US distributors (3 buyer consortia hold most purchasing) -> pharmacy. India: company -> stockist -> chemist, with doctor prescription the moat. Margins: innovator/specialty > complex generics > India brands > oral solids US > API.

**Cycle drivers:** US generic price erosion, FDA compliance cycles, blockbuster LOE waves, China API pricing, US trade policy (Section 232, Biosecure), India price control (NLEM/DPCO).

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- USFDA warning letters / Form 483 / import alerts (FDA data dashboard)
- AIOCD-AWACS monthly IPM growth
- IQVIA US generic pricing
- China API price trackers
- US Commerce Section 232 reviews (generics review due by ~Apr 2027)

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: specialty/complex portfolio, India brand strength, clean FDA record, disciplined capital allocation. Losers: FDA import alerts, overpaying for US generics assets (2015–17), one-product (gRevlimid) earnings capitalised at full multiple.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/E 20–35x; CDMO 40–70x. Peaks: 2015 (US boom) and Aug 2020 (COVID). Trough: 2018–19 (erosion + FDA). Pharma was the only large-cap sector above its FY26 average valuation in 2026 (5paisa).

**Current state (Nov 2026):** Q2 FY27 preview: US segment for some large caps seen −15% YoY on gRevlimid fade and erosion; Sun US sales $427m Q1 FY27 vs $473m. Section 232 (2 Apr 2026): 100% tariff on patented drugs, generics exempt for now, with a review within a year; a phased generic tariff was floated in Jul 2026 (status unverified).

**Classic traps:**
- Capitalising one-off exclusivity profits
- Ignoring FDA site concentration
- CDMO 'pipeline' that never commercialises
- Generic tariff tail risk at the Section 232 review

**Hidden trap: Manpasand's growth faster than Frooti** (`case_study:hidden-trap-manpasand-growth`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: a mango-drink maker (Mango Sip) growing 33-44% in FY18, faster than Parle Agro's Frooti, with Q4 FY18 profit +256% to Rs 43 cr; marquee fund holders; big new plant capex. WHY IT LIED: GST investigators found sales inflated through invoices to bogus firms with no goods moving (outward bogus transactions ~Rs 691 cr, inward ~Rs 188 cr); MD and officials arrested in 2019 in a ~Rs 40 cr tax fraud; FY19 revenue fell 33% with a receivables write-off. TELLS: (1) a small brand outgrowing the category leader in a mature, distribution-heavy category is physically unlikely; a fund manager publicly questioned growth and market share in Dec 2016; (2) trade receivables growing faster than sales [commentary estimate ~40% vs ~25%, unverified]; (3) Deloitte resigned in May 2018 citing denial of revenue and capex data; the next auditor quit in 2019. TEST: compare growth with the category and the leader; ask for distributor counts and channel checks (shop visits); match capex to physical capacity; treat an auditor citing denied information as a disqualifier. LESSON: growth that beats the industry's best operator without a visible mechanism (new channel, technology, price) is a question, not a strength.

**Hidden trap: Vakrangee's 40% ROCE, zero debt and positive CFO** (`case_study:hidden-trap-vakrangee-roce-debt-free`, single-source). THE GOOD NUMBER: screener-perfect: ROCE 37-43%, OPM ~25%, borrowings cut from Rs 416 cr (FY15) to zero (FY18), PAT Rs 322 -> 680 cr in three years, and CFO was positive and above PAT in FY17-18 (Rs 669 cr, Rs 530 cr), so even our CFO/PAT test passed. The stock ran to ~Rs 515 (Jan 2018). WHY IT LIED: a network of franchised rural kiosks for banking, e-governance and e-commerce is a thin-margin, low-ticket business; 25% operating margins and 40% ROCE were out of line with every comparable. In FY18 sales jumped 63% to Rs 6,502 cr while OPM fell from 24% to 15%, signalling a mix shift into low-value trading. Debtor days were 157 in FY15. PwC resigned in Apr 2018; the stock fell ~84%; FY19 revenue collapsed to Rs 1,508 cr and debtor days went to 319, 729 and 1,301 (FY19-21). It trades at ~Rs 5 (Nov 2026). TEST: rebuild unit economics bottom-up (revenue per outlet x outlets x margin) and compare with the reported total; treat a sudden revenue-mix shift plus a parabolic price as a request for evidence. LESSON: CFO/PAT can pass in a trap; numbers that are too good for the business's physics are a flag on their own.
